abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) elevates joint audio-video generation, but optimizing heterogeneous, modality-specific audio and video rewards often introduces cross-modal interference. On-policy distillation (OPD) alleviates this issue by transferring the capabilities of specialized audio and video RL teachers into a single student model. However, a significant imbalance in cross-modal token counts leaves audio with sparse supervision, causing unstable distillation. We observe that naively increasing the audio loss weight fails to solve this problem since audio learning relies heavily on visual context, indicating richer visual cues are crucial to offset sparse audio signals. To address this, we propose OmniOPD, a modality-wise on-policy distillation framework designed for balanced and stable audio-video generation. First, we construct privileged visual information using asymmetric noise scheduling, allowing the audio teacher to generate more informative targets from cleaner video context. Second, we introduce grouped multi-noise sampling to expand audio supervision coverage and stabilize training. Third, we introduce timestep-wise importance weighting based on teacher-student transition divergence, preserving reliable supervision while down-weighting unreliable learning signals, to stabilize fluctuations in audio learning. Evaluated on JavisBench and VBench demonstrate OmniOPD preserves audio quality while significantly enhancing video generation, achieving effective joint distillation.

sections.body: The introduction states that jointly optimizing audio and video rewards causes cross-modal interference and imbalanced gradients. Audio occupies substantially fewer tokens than video, which leaves it with sparse supervision in on-policy distillation. The authors report that audio-only RL is unstable and degrades video quality (Fig. 1), and that video-first optimization stabilizes audio learning (Fig. 2). OmniOPD adds privileged visual guidance, grouped multi-noise sampling, and timestep-wise importance weighting. The stated contributions are analysis, the method, and experiments showing stabilized distillation with gains in audio quality, video quality, and synchronization.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Joint audio-video training with multiple rewards causes interference, so the authors propose OmniOPD, a modality-wise distillation framework.

sections.body: The related work groups prior research into three areas. Joint audio-video generation includes MM-Diffusion, JavisDiT, UniVerse-1, and LTX-2. Reinforcement learning for generative models includes DDPO, Flow-GRPO, GDPO, DiffusionNFT, and OmniNFT, the last of which extends this to joint audio-video generation. On-policy distillation work includes MOPD, Open-MOPD, TrOPD, Flow-OPD, and DiffusionOPD. The section states that OmniOPD builds on vanilla OPD to stabilize joint audio-video distillation and that prior work does not address this stabilization.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior work covers joint audio-video generators, RL for generative models, and on-policy distillation, and OmniOPD builds on vanilla OPD.

sections.body: The motivation section reports three observations from Fig. 2. Audio-only reward optimization shows unstable training, with audio quality and video quality both declining. Joint-reward optimization yields limited gains, and increasing audio reward weights can further degrade both modalities. Optimizing video first and then audio substantially alleviates the instability seen in audio-only optimization. The authors conclude that sparse and unstable audio supervision is the main bottleneck and that cleaner visual context can help. These observations motivate the three components of OmniOPD.
sections.heading: Motivation
sections.headline: Audio-only reward optimization is unstable and degrades video, and raising audio reward weights does not fix the imbalance.

sections.body: The preliminaries define a joint flow-matching model with audio and video latents, where each modality is perturbed by a Gaussian endpoint at a shared timestep. The flow-matching loss is summed over the audio and video modalities. On-policy distillation is defined as matching the student and teacher one-step transition kernels along student-generated trajectories. For the stochastic flow transitions in Flow-OPD, the local divergence is written with a time-adaptive scaling factor $w(t)$. Figure 3 gives an overview of the frozen teachers, the privileged visual guidance, multi-noise sampling, and state-reliability weighting.
sections.heading: Preliminaries
sections.headline: The section defines joint audio-video flow matching and the on-policy distillation objective, then shows the OmniOPD overview.

sections.body: The method section formulates a clean-prediction distillation loss for each modality. Privileged visual guidance gives the audio teacher a cleaner video input at a lower noise level $q(t)$ while the student and teacher share the same audio state. Multi-noise audio distillation samples $G$ trajectories per prompt and averages the audio loss over them. Timestep-wise importance weighting computes a transition divergence $D_{g}(t)$ and applies a stop-gradient weight that keeps full supervision within a trust region set by $\kappa$. The final objective adds this weighted audio loss to the video distillation loss. The section gives no numerical results.
sections.heading: OmniOPD
sections.headline: OmniOPD adds asymmetric visual noise for the audio teacher, grouped audio sampling, and a trust-region importance weight.

sections.body: Table 1 reports JavisBench results. OmniOPD reaches VQ 3.347 and TA-IB 0.192, but its AQ of 5.449 is below the Audio-Teacher's 5.576, and its DeSync of 0.457 is above the Audio-Teacher's 0.448. Table 2 compares against Vanilla OPD, which has VQ 3.174 and DeSync 0.583, and against Cascade, which has DeSync 0.432. The ablations in Table 3 vary the shift strategy for teacher video noise, the number of branches $G$, and the weighting strength. The authors report that cleaner visual context and more branches improve audio quality, and that weighting reduces the video degradation. The section does not report variance or significance tests.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: On JavisBench, OmniOPD gives the highest video quality among distilled models and stronger audio text alignment, with ablations on guidance, coverage, and weighting.

sections.body: The conclusion summarizes the analysis of audio-video coupling, which shows cross-modal interference and sparse, stochastic audio supervision. OmniOPD combines asymmetric supervision, privileged visual guidance, and reliability-aware multi-branch learning. The authors state that experiments on JavisBench and VBench show improved video generation alongside strong audio performance. The conclusion does not restate limits, which appear in the appendix.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: OmniOPD stabilizes joint audio-video distillation and improves video generation while keeping strong audio performance.

sections.body: The derivation shows that transition divergence equals a clean-prediction regression with a schedule-dependent coefficient $\bar{w}(t)$. The authors note that dropping this coefficient changes the weighting across timesteps, so the objective becomes a surrogate rather than an identical KL objective. The limitations state that teachers see student-generated states that may differ from their training distribution, and that their predictions can become unreliable when those states fall outside their supported distributions. The appendix also lists the four evaluation prompts for Fig. 4 and presents additional qualitative examples in Figs. 6 and 7.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix derives the link between transition divergence and clean-prediction regression, then states limitations and lists qualitative examples.
